thread:
asha: Hey team — Acme reported sporadic 400 errors from the embeddings endpoint and a huge tail latency spike last night (p95 fine, p99 ~12s). They say errors mention 'embedding dimension mismatch' sometimes and other times requests just time out. Anyone seen this pattern?

kai: Can you paste an example request payload from the customer logs? exact shape and dims pls.

asha: Pasted below (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-redwood-1024",
  "input": ["short text", "longer chunk...", "..."],
  "batching": {"max_batch_size": 64, "dynamic": true}
}
```

ravi: Looks normal. The model expects 1024 dims. Are they mixing inputs from two clients? dimension mismatch usually means the stored vector or schema doesn't match returned size during post-processing.

asha: Customer says they call same endpoint from multiple services behind a proxy; no pre-embedding. Errors are intermittent — ~1 in 200 requests.

elliot: Could be dynamic batching coalescing inputs across model variants? If some requests are routed to a trimmed quantized variant with 768-dim output and postprocessing assumes 1024, that yields mismatch.

kai: Good call. Check routing logs for model variant selection during that window (02:10–03:00 UTC). ops-bot, pull routing trace for request IDs from Acme during that window.

ops-bot: Retrieved 37 traces for customer acct acme-corp between 1965547200 and 1965550800. 5 traces routed to model-embed-768-quant, 32 routed to embed-1024-fp16.

ravi: There we go. Why would routing pick the 768 variant though? It should only pick compatible variants. Maybe fallback policy allowed lower-dim if capacity constrained.

asha: Customer says they didn't change client model param; always requests "embed-redwood-1024".

kai: Check the smart routing policy for that tenant during spikes: maybe autoscaling throttled 1024 pool and fallback was allowed. Also dynamic batching could coalesce different model requests if not checking model_id per-batch.

elliot: I just grep'd the batching logs: found a batch where requests for model embed-redwood-1024 and embed-redwood-768 ended up in same dynamic batch due to a bug in batch-key hashing when request metadata was missing.

asha: That would cause both kinds to run on the same execution path — downstream postprocessing sees mismatched dims. Any idea how often metadata missing happens?

ravi: Metadata missing occurs when the customer uses an older SDK that doesn't set the model header in the internal proxy. We saw a handful of mobile clients doing that last month.

kai: Root cause hypothesis: older SDK => missing model header => batching key collision across variants => single batch executed on 768 variant when mixed => some outputs 768 dims but caller expected 1024 => dimension mismatch errors. Tail latency: coalesced batches included long-running requests and small ones, and when the 1024 pool was cold/scale-limited, batches waited up to 8–10s to fill causing p99 spikes.

asha: Next steps for support: 1) temporary mitigation — force per-tenant strict model affinity (no fallback) for Acme so their requests always route to 1024 variant; 2) disable dynamic batching across variants globally until we patch batch-key hashing.

kai: Agreed. I'll push a config flip for tenant-level routing affinity and a global emergency flag to isolate model ids before batching. ETA 10m.

ops-bot: Deploying config change: set tenant.acme-corp.routing.affinity = true (by kai). Rolling to 3 control-plane nodes.

ops-bot: Global batching isolation flag set: batching.isolate_by_model = true (by kai).

asha: Customer applied a short retry with backoff on their side and says errors stopped immediately after your changes. Tail latencies dropped to normal 90s after the isolation flag. :thumbsup:

ravi: We still need a permanent fix: patch the batch-key generation to include model_id and quantization tag and add a defensive assertion in the postprocess to fail earlier with clear logs when dims don't match. Also add a per-tenant config check to warn when SDK header missing.

elliot: I'll open a runtime PR for the batch-key fix and add unit tests for mixed-variant coalescing. Also will add an integration test simulating older SDK requests missing header.

kai: For rollout: canary the batch-key fix with batching.isolate_by_model=false in staging, validate no cross-variant batches, then schedule prod rollout next week. Add a feature gate to revert quickly.

asha: Support action items after this thread: confirm customer stable for 24h, provide RCA draft, and recommend they upgrade SDK. I'll send them a short postmortem and temporary mitigation summary.

ops-bot: Alert: 1 active follow-up (support ticket #1423) created for acme-corp.

ravi: Also propose metrics: add an alert if any "dimension_mismatch" error rate > 0.1% over 5m and an internal tracing span that tags model_id used vs requested.

kai: I'll add a dashboard tile showing per-variant routing ratios per tenant and a p99 latency breakdown by batch size.

asha: Thanks everyone. Marking thread resolved for now; reopen if Acme sees a recurrence.

elliot: PR links for reference: runtime batch-key fix (WIP) -> https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4182; integration test -> https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4183

asha: Closing comments: please add postmortem with timeline once PR merged.

ops-bot: Thread archived (by ops-bot).
